correctness.rationale: For a+b=2h>0, season half-width t=T/2>0, g>0 and real mean r, both seasonal matrices have trace 2(r-h). Their traceless parts M1,M2 satisfy M1²=κ_-²I, M2²=κ_+²I and half tr(M2M1)=h²-g², giving the exact normalized monodromy half-trace C_p(t) with p=ab. The rational Laplace identity C_hat=s/(s²-4h²)[1-16g²p/((s²-4h²)(s²-4g²))]^{-1} yields a Volterra series in p with nonnegative causal kernel and strictly positive convolution coefficients at t>0. Thus C_p(t)>C_0(t)=cosh(2ht)>1 for p>0, strictly increasing for p from zero to h², and λ=r-h+T^{-1}arcosh C_p(T/2) increases strictly. Balancing a=b uniquely maximizes; one-way boundaries both give λ=r. For r<0 a viability threshold exists iff balanced λ>0, with unique p_* solving C=cosh((h-r)T); critical equality covered. Taylor fourth coefficient C_p−cosh(2ht)=(2/3)g²p t⁴+O(t⁶) produces λ−r=g²p T²/(24h)+O(T⁴). Independent scipy matrix exponentials for h=g=1,T=4,r=-1/5 reproduce endpoint -0.2, imbalanced -0.0024963625 and balanced +0.0426584316. Finite values are only corroboration.

originality.rationale: PASS on the sharp fixed-total-transport-rate directional balancing law for equal-mean exactly antiphase square waves. The most relevant Benaïm et al 2023 primary paper treats non-symmetric migration but its §4.3 compares fixed migration direction and varying scalar intensity with unequal local means; it shows numerical Floquet curves, not a theorem that at fixed a+b all periods and contrasts optimize at a=b. Supplementary S1 concerns three-patch directional migration. Broader growth criteria do not imply this strict p=ab ordering. Specialized equivalent spectral inequalities remain a realistic but not decisive priority risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed two-season Floquet trace inequality could imply this specialized monotonicity.
Strictness requires g,h,T>0 and equal-duration exact antiphase seasons; at g=0 strict inequality fails.
Growth exponent is not an unconditional nonlinear persistence theorem.
